extracted.intended_audience: investor relations professionals, corporate communications teams, and compliance officers at public (and capital-raising private) companies
extracted.subtask_short: investor relations compliance for public companies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for investor relations (IR) teams to meet SEC, FINRA, CFTC and other regulatory requirements, manage material non-public information, maintain records, and run a digital-first compliance program for investor communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation Fair Disclosure (Reg FD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevents selective disclosure by requiring companies to share material information with all investors simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures a level playing field and prevents insider advantages; applicable to earnings calls, investor briefings and other disclosures—virtual events should be made accessible to all investors to comply with Reg FD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (periodic reporting: Forms 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandates periodic reporting to keep investors informed about financial performance, risks, and material events via Forms 10‑K, 10‑Q and 8‑K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IR teams must ensure timely, accurate filings that reflect company performance and material developments; incorporate information from filings into other investor communications to avoid contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) corporate governance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduces corporate governance requirements including financial reporting controls, auditor independence, and CEO/CFO certification of financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IR communications must align with SOX-controlled financial reporting and internal control regimes; ensure disclosures reflect certified financial data and support auditor and governance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC Rule 10b-5 (anti-fraud in disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits misleading statements, material omissions, and fraudulent activities in securities trading and disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central rule to prevent investor deception—IR content must avoid misstatements and omissions; factual accuracy and completeness are required across press releases, presentations, and investor conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must determine what information is 'material' (i.e., information that could influence an investor’s decision) and disclose it promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a consistent process to assess materiality for events, results, or changes; coordinate legal, finance, and IR to decide disclosure timing and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Accessibility of Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures should be easy to understand and accessible via company websites, investor portals, and SEC filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language, clear formatting and multiple channels (website, filings, investor portal) so investors of varying sophistication can access and comprehend disclosure information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GAAP and Non-GAAP Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-GAAP financial metrics can help investors understand performance, but must be presented with clear reconciliation to GAAP measures and cannot be misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always provide reconciliations and avoid presenting non-GAAP metrics in a way that obscures GAAP results; ensure consistent presentation across materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency Across Communication Channels
rubrics_metrics.description: All investor-facing materials (press releases, earnings calls, presentations) must align to prevent contradictory messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate messaging across PR, IR, investor presentations and filings; pre-approve and reconcile content to avoid regulatory scrutiny from inconsistent statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Management of Material Non-Public Information (MNPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material non-public information refers to confidential data that, if disclosed, could influence an investor’s decision to buy or sell securities (examples: upcoming earnings, M&A activity, regulatory investigations, leadership changes, major contracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify MNPI categories, log instances, and ensure controls are in place to prevent unauthorized disclosure; treat MNPI as the core risk IR must protect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider Trading Policies and Trading Blackout Periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish clear rules on when employees can trade company securities and enforce trading blackout periods before major announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement pre-clearance processes, defined blackout windows around earnings/major events, and sanctions for violations to reduce insider trading risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Barriers (restrict access to MNPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict access to sensitive financial data, ensuring that only authorized personnel can view confidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use role-based access, need-to-know permissions, and physical/digital separation between teams to limit MNPI exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee Training on Unauthorized Disclosures and Insider Trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate employees on the legal consequences of unauthorized disclosures and insider trading violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run regular training for IR, executives, finance and other staff; include scenario-based modules and refresh training when regulations or processes change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor Communications to Prevent Accidental Leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Review emails, internal messages, and investor interactions to prevent accidental leaks of MNPI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement proactive monitoring (manual review and automated monitoring tools) for internal and external communications to detect potential violations or inadvertent disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Documentation and Record-Keeping Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory agencies (SEC, FINRA, CFTC) require companies to maintain thorough records of investor communications and financial disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain documentation to demonstrate regulatory compliance, provide audit trails, and support dispute resolution; ensure records are organized, searchable and defensible in audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Retention Policies and Specific Rules (SEC Rule 17a-4; FINRA Rule 4511)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow legally required retention periods for records (the page references SEC Rule 17a-4 as mandating a minimum five-year retention for certain records and elsewhere references SEC Rule 17a-4 and FINRA Rule 4511 as mandating at least six years, with some records readily accessible for the first two years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt conservative retention schedules that meet or exceed applicable rules; ensure quick accessibility for records required to be readily available during initial periods (e.g., first two years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Record Storage (secure digital archives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Store financial statements, earnings reports, and investor communications in compliance-approved formats for easy retrieval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use secure, compliance-approved storage with indexing and search capabilities; retain records in formats accepted for regulatory inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Record-Keeping and Archiving Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Use compliance software to log and track disclosures, press releases, and investor interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automate capture and retention of communications to reduce human error, maintain consistent metadata, and facilitate audits and e‑discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Communication Monitoring (social media, email, messaging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Firms must track digital investor interactions—including social media posts, emails, and messaging platforms—to ensure compliance with financial disclosure laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archive social posts, pre-approve investor-facing social content, and monitor channels for unauthorized statements; integrate social and messaging capture into record-keeping systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Trails for Investor Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining a clear audit trail helps companies verify that disclosures were made in accordance with SEC and FINRA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record decision-making, approvals, timestamps and distribution lists for disclosures so actions can be reconstructed during audits or investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Policies and Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish clear internal policies covering investor disclosures, digital communication guidelines, and MNPI handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document processes, roles, and responsibilities; keep policy manuals up to date and ensure employees know where to find them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and Oversight Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a system where financial disclosures, press releases, and investor materials undergo compliance review before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require sign-offs from IR, legal, and finance as appropriate; maintain version control and approval logs to evidence oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and Education as a Component of Compliance Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly educate IR professionals, executives, and employees on compliance risks, regulatory updates, and best practices for digital communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule periodic trainings and update sessions tied to regulatory changes; test understanding and track completion for compliance records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media Compliance for Investor Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms like LinkedIn and Twitter must comply with SEC and FINRA guidelines; investor-related posts should be pre-approved, archived, and aligned with official disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-clear posts, coordinate messaging with filings, and ensure social content is captured in retention systems to meet regulatory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email and Messaging Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Investor updates via email must follow regulatory requirements, with firms retaining records in accordance with SEC Rule 17a-4 and FINRA Rule 4511.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure templates and distribution lists are controlled, archives capture inbound/outbound messages, and sensitive information is not shared outside approved channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Webinars and Virtual Investor Events Recording & Transcription
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings calls, investor briefings, and virtual roadshows should be recorded, transcribed, and made accessible to all investors to comply with Reg FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish recordings/transcripts promptly, archive them for retention periods, and ensure simultaneous access where required to avoid selective disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-Powered Compliance Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies are adopting technology solutions to monitor digital communications in real-time, flagging potential regulatory breaches before they escalate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy automated monitoring to surface risky language or disclosure patterns; integrate alerts into compliance workflows for rapid response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving and Record-Keeping Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated solutions ensure all investor communications are securely stored and easily retrievable for audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select platforms that provide tamper-evident archives, searchability, retention controls, and export capabilities for regulatory inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Dashboards and Real-Time Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time monitoring tools provide oversight of digital engagement, highlighting potential non-compliant activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dashboards to synthesize risk indicators, track open issues, and demonstrate proactive supervision to regulators and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Disclosure Management
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-driven platforms assist in drafting, reviewing, and distributing investor disclosures in accordance with regulatory guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage automation to standardize disclosures and ensure required reconciliations and approvals are in place prior to distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Compliance, Risk Management, and Security
rubrics_metrics.description: Align compliance efforts with broader risk management and security initiatives to protect sensitive information while meeting regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate legal, finance, compliance and IT to ensure controls, incident response, and retention policies are consistent and mutually reinforcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Encryption and Access Controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect investor-related communications with encryption and limit access to authorized personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement encryption at rest/in transit, strong authentication and least-privilege access for systems containing MNPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity Policies for IR Teams
rubrics_metrics.description: IR professionals should follow secure communication practices, such as avoiding unapproved messaging platforms and using multi-factor authentication (MFA) for data access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain approved tools list, require MFA, and enforce secure endpoints and networks for remote work and virtual events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Response and Crisis Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a structured plan for handling security breaches or compliance violations to mitigate risks and maintain transparency with investors and regulators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define escalation paths, communication protocols and remediation steps; rehearse incident scenarios and document lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular Compliance Audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct periodic internal audits to detect gaps in disclosure procedures, investor communications, and digital record-keeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule audits at least annually or when there are material changes; document findings and remediate gaps promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation Protocols for Compliance Breaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly defined response plans ensure that compliance breaches, such as unauthorized disclosures, are handled swiftly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish who to notify internally and externally, timing expectations for regulator/investor communications, and post-incident review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor Regulatory Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws and regulations evolve; staying updated on SEC, FINRA, and CFTC rule changes minimizes compliance risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain regulatory watch processes, subscribe to updates, and update policies/procedures and training when rules change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Department Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal, finance, compliance, and IT teams should work together to ensure that compliance efforts align with security protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create formal governance forums and joint workflows so disclosures, technical controls and legal analyses are coordinated before public statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Risk Monitoring and Regulatory Reporting Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralized platforms for compliance reporting help organizations document and track compliance actions and improve audit readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement tools that aggregate incidents, track remediation, and produce regulator-ready reports; use analytics to detect unusual investor interactions or trading patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize Analytical Discipline Over PR 'Hype'
rubrics_metrics.description: Investor relations should assess financial results with an analyst’s eye and ensure disclosures reflect investment credentials rather than promotional spin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating IR as marketing—emphasize accuracy, context and investor value rather than promotional messaging that could mislead or invite regulatory scrutiny.
